title: Keep width and min-width within the smallest viewport

values: any file that can contain a stylesheet, a <style> block, a style attribute or a JSX style object (e.g. .css, .html, .jsx, .tsx, JSX-bearing .js/.ts, and any other such file)
facts.note: Semantic, non-exhaustive candidate set: governed by declaration context, not by a closed extension list. Extensions only narrow candidates; any file containing a governed context is in scope. Candidacy alone does not show a width declaration exists.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.

values: bun_responsive_detector: width/min-width (CSS) or width/minWidth (JSX style object), existing or new, in a stylesheet, <style> block, style attribute or JSX style object exceeds smallest frontend.viewports width
facts.note: Requires content inspection (parsing stylesheets, style blocks, style attributes, JSX style objects), rem/em at 16px, compared with the smallest configured viewport (default 375px). Applies to all present declarations, not only changed ones.

fires: A stylesheet declares `width: 1200px` on a page container while the smallest configured viewport is below 1200px (e.g. default 375px).
A JSX style object (in a .jsx, .tsx or JSX-bearing .js file) sets `minWidth` to a value above the smallest configured viewport (e.g. 30rem = 480px > 375px).
A pre-existing `style` attribute or `<style>` block sets `min-width` wider than the smallest entry in `frontend.viewports`.
doesNotFire: A declaration uses `max-width: 1200px` to cap a wide layout.
A custom property definition such as `--page: 1200px` defines a token.
An oversized width appears inside `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` or `_generated`.
A `width` at or below the smallest configured viewport (e.g. `width: 320px` with default 375px).

given: A stylesheet, `<style>` block, `style` attribute or JSX `style` object (in any file) outside vendored/generated trees
then: The value (rem/em at 16px) MUST NOT exceed the smallest width in `atdd-bun.yaml` `frontend.viewports` (default 375px).
prefer: Make content fluid at small viewports, usually `width: 100%` plus an appropriate `max-width`, not an oversized fixed `width`/`min-width`.
Express wide layouts with `max-width`, percentages, or wrapping layouts.
During GREEN: fix only the element responsible for the current overflow; reuse existing layout containers and responsive primitives.
During GREEN: keep the intended large-screen cap while letting the element shrink.
Config (frontend_settings): `frontend.viewports` = widths responsive specs render at (smallest bounds fixed widths); `frontend.breakpoints` = widths media queries may use.
avoid: Hiding overflow to mask an oversized element.
Removing useful `max-width` constraints merely to pass the detector.
unless: `max-width` is not judged; it is how wide layouts are bounded.
Custom property definitions (`--page: 1200px`) are tokens, not judged.
why: An element wider than the screen forces horizontal scrolling on every phone.
evidence: The current responsive acceptance passes at the smallest governed viewport.
The affected declaration no longer forces horizontal overflow (established on its own, not inferred from detector silence).
bun_responsive_detector reports no finding for the declaration.
verifier_detail: Scan `width` and `min-width` declarations (JSX camelCase `minWidth`) in stylesheets, `<style>` blocks, `style` attributes and JSX `style` objects in any file that contains them (not limited to a fixed extension list; includes JSX-bearing .js/.ts); convert `rem` and `em` at 16px; finding if value > smallest width in `atdd-bun.yaml` `frontend.viewports` (default 375px).
Skip `max-width` declarations and custom property definitions (`--name: value`).
Term frontend_settings: `atdd-bun.yaml` → `frontend.viewports` (the widths responsive specs render at; the smallest bounds fixed widths) and `frontend.breakpoints` (the widths media queries may use).

additions.justification: Illustrates the threshold boundary derived directly from the statement; no new obligation.
The source's JSX style object context implies the camelCase property; spelled out so it is not overlooked. No new obligation.

additions.text: bun_responsive_detector reports no finding for the declaration.
additions.justification: Follows from the source's validator implementation and strict disposition; kept separate from the overflow proof (evidence[1]) so detector silence is not treated as proof of no overflow.
Lossless placement of the frontend_settings definition (S009) in a coder-facing field.
